title: Apps cannot use the microphone because Windows privacy settings block access
symptoms: The microphone works in Sound settings, but apps say no microphone is found or access is denied
Desktop apps such as Teams, Zoom, Discord or a browser cannot hear me
The microphone stopped working in apps after an update or a privacy reset
causes: Microphone access is turned off for the whole device
'Let apps access your microphone' is turned off, or the specific Store app is turned off
'Let desktop apps access your microphone' is turned off, which blocks all classic desktop apps

signals: Privacy setting for microphone access (device-wide, apps, or desktop apps) is set to Deny/Off
Recording endpoint is active and shows signal, but apps report no access

fixes.title: Turn on microphone access for Windows, apps and desktop apps
steps: Open Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone (Windows 10: Settings > Privacy > Microphone).
Turn on Microphone access (Windows 10: select Change and turn on access for this device).
Turn on Let apps access your microphone, and turn on each app that needs the microphone.
Scroll down and turn on Let desktop apps access your microphone.
If the microphone is built into a webcam, also check Settings > Privacy & security > Camera.
Restart the app that could not use the microphone and test again.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft troubleshooting page (Windows 10 and 11 steps)
Dell KB 'Microphone Not Working Due to Privacy Settings in Windows 11 or Windows 10'
Dell self-support microphone guide; notes desktop apps cannot be allowed individually

title: Microphone not detected or not listed as an input device
symptoms: No microphone appears under Sound > Input
Windows says no input devices were found
The microphone is plugged in but the input level bar never moves
causes: A different input device is set as the default
The microphone endpoint is disabled and hidden in the classic Sound control panel
The audio or microphone driver is missing or corrupted

signals: No active capture (recording) endpoint exists, or the default capture endpoint is not the expected device
A capture endpoint exists in a Disabled state
An audio device in Device Manager shows an error code or is missing

fixes.title: Select the microphone as the input device and test it
steps: Check that the microphone or headset mute button is off and the cable or Bluetooth connection is in place.
Open Settings > System > Sound.
Under Input, choose your microphone under 'Choose a device for speaking or recording' (Windows 10: 'Choose your input device').
Open the device page and select Start test, speak, then stop the test to check the level.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft troubleshooting page
Dell self-support microphone guide: select input device under Sound > Input

fixes.title: Show disabled recording devices and enable the microphone
steps: Open Settings > System > Sound > More sound settings, or press Win+R and run mmsys.cpl.
Open the Recording tab.
Right-click an empty area of the list and select Show Disabled Devices and Show Disconnected Devices.
If the microphone appears greyed out, right-click it and select Enable.
Right-click it again and select Set as Default Device, then speak and watch the level bars.

sources.signal: Microsoft Q&A, answer accepted by question author; steps answer has 6 helpful votes

fixes.title: Run the recording audio troubleshooter
steps: Windows 11: open Settings > System > Sound, scroll to Advanced, and select Input devices under 'Troubleshoot common sound problems'.
Windows 10: open Settings > Update & Security > Troubleshoot > Additional troubleshooters and run Recording Audio.
Select the microphone that is not working and follow the prompts.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft troubleshooting page
Dell self-support microphone guide: Sound > Advanced > Input devices troubleshooter

fixes.title: Uninstall the audio or microphone device and let Windows reinstall it
steps: Right-click Start and select Device Manager.
Expand Sound, video and game controllers (for USB microphones, also Audio inputs and outputs).
Right-click the audio device or microphone and select Uninstall device, then select Uninstall.
Restart the PC so Windows reinstalls the device.
If it does not come back, right-click the category in Device Manager and select Scan for hardware changes.
If it still fails, right-click the device and select Update driver, or install the driver from the PC or microphone maker.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft troubleshooting page, 'Windows doesn't detect the mic' section

Dell self-support microphone guide: update driver under Audio inputs and outputs

title: Microphone volume too low or others can barely hear me
symptoms: People on calls say my voice is very quiet
The input level bar barely moves when I speak
Recordings are much quieter than expected
causes: Input volume slider or Levels setting is low
Microphone Boost is set to 0 dB on mics that support it
Audio enhancements on the input device lower or process the signal

signals: Default capture endpoint volume is well below 100%

fixes.title: Raise the input volume and Microphone Boost
steps: Open Settings > System > Sound and select your microphone under Input.
Raise the Input volume slider, then use Start test to check the level.
For more control, press Win+R, run mmsys.cpl, open the Recording tab, and open the microphone's Properties.
On the Levels tab, set Microphone to 100 and, if a Microphone Boost slider exists, raise it in small steps (for example +10 dB).
Lower the boost again if you hear hiss or distortion.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft page: 'Volume is too low' section, Levels tab Microphone and Microphone Boost sliders
Microsoft Q&A, answer accepted by question author; asker confirmed mic returned to usual levels
Dell self-support guide: raise Input slider in small steps to avoid distortion

fixes.title: Turn off audio enhancements for the microphone
steps: Open Settings > System > Sound and select the microphone under Input.
Turn off Audio enhancements if the option is shown.
Or run mmsys.cpl, open the Recording tab, open the microphone's Properties, and on the Enhancements or Advanced tab disable all enhancements.
Test the microphone again.

sources.signal: Dell self-support guide: turn off audio enhancements in device properties
Microsoft Q&A, answer accepted by question author; asker confirmed

title: Microphone works in one app but not another, or its level changes by itself
symptoms: The microphone works in one app but another app hears nothing or says the device is in use
The microphone stops working in other apps while a call or game is open
The microphone input level moves up or down on its own
causes: One app has taken exclusive control of the microphone
Apps are allowed to change the microphone level through exclusive mode
Desktop apps are blocked in privacy settings while Store apps are allowed

signals: Capture endpoint has 'Allow applications to take exclusive control of this device' enabled
Capture endpoint volume changes without user action while an app is running
Desktop-app microphone access is Off while Store-app access is On

fixes.title: Make sure desktop apps are allowed to use the microphone
steps: Open Settings > Privacy & security > Microphone.
Turn on Let desktop apps access your microphone.
Restart the app that cannot use the microphone.

sources.signal: Official Microsoft troubleshooting page
Dell KB on microphone privacy settings

fixes.title: Stop apps from taking exclusive control of the microphone
steps: Press Win+R, run mmsys.cpl, and open the Recording tab.
Right-click the microphone and select Properties.
On the Advanced tab, clear 'Allow applications to take exclusive control of this device'.
Also clear 'Give exclusive mode applications priority', then select OK.
Close and reopen the apps that use the microphone.

title: Headset microphone not working on a laptop's combined headphone/mic jack
symptoms: Headset audio plays, but Windows still uses the laptop's built-in microphone
The headset microphone never appears as an input device
No pop-up asks what kind of device was plugged in
causes: The jack is set to Headphones instead of Headset (with microphone) in the Realtek or Waves MaxxAudio app
On Dell laptops, the Waves MaxxAudio service that handles jack detection is not running
The headset uses a plug that is not compatible with the combo jack (needs a 4-pole TRRS plug)

signals: A headphone render endpoint becomes active on plug-in but no new capture endpoint appears
Realtek audio driver is installed and the device has a single 3.5 mm combo jack

fixes.title: Set the jack to Headset (with microphone) in the audio app
steps: Plug the headset into the combo jack.
If a pop-up asks what device you plugged in, choose Headset (not Headphones) and select OK; do not select 'Never show this dialog again'.
If no pop-up appears, open Realtek Audio Console from Start, select Device advanced settings, and under Connector Retasking (Analog) choose Headset or 'Headset (with microphone)'.
On Dell laptops with Waves MaxxAudio, check that the Waves MaxxAudio Service Application is enabled, restart with the headset unplugged, then plug it in and choose the headset in the prompt.
Open Settings > System > Sound and pick the headset microphone under Input, then test it.

sources.signal: Dell KB: enable Waves MaxxAudio service, reboot unplugged, select correct device in prompt

Microsoft Q&A answer with 5 helpful votes (not accepted): Realtek Audio Console > Device advanced settings > Connector Retasking > Headset
